backbone: EfficientNet-B0 (pretrained=False at inference load time to ensure offline independence)
input_modality: Single RGB retinal fundus photograph (normalized to 224x224)

task_heads.head: cvd
task_heads.target: Cardiovascular Disease (vascular disease or myocardial infarction history)

task_heads.head: dr
task_heads.target: Diabetic Retinopathy ICDR Grade (0: No DR, 1: Mild, 2: Moderate, 3: Severe, 4: Proliferative)
task_heads.threshold: Argmax with confidence threshold (>= 0.50 and margin >= 0.15)

dataset.name: mBRSET (Mobile Brazilian Retinal Dataset)
dataset.cohort_size: 1,289 patients with verified retinal images on disk (1,268 eligible for CVD analysis)
dataset.cohort_composition: Diabetic patients attending clinical centers in Brazil
dataset.camera_type: Phelcom Eyer (handheld smartphone-based non-mydriatic retinal camera)

known_limitations_and_clinical_caveats: Single-source cohort: trained exclusively on mBRSET with no external hospital validation.
Cohort homogeneity: essentially all patients have diagnosed diabetes mellitus; the system cannot classify or predict diabetes status.
Retinal finding vs diagnosis: Diabetic Retinopathy grade is a microvascular retinal finding, not a systemic diagnosis of diabetes.
No numeric blood pressure: the dataset provides binary hypertension history, not continuous systolic/diastolic values.
Historical target: CVD labels reflect self/clinician-reported history of vascular disease or myocardial infarction, not prospective 5- or 10-year incident risk.
Low CVD discriminative performance: image-only CVD prediction is near chance level (~0.56 ROC-AUC in held-out test split).
Domain specificity: images were acquired with handheld Phelcom Eyer cameras; generalizability to desktop fundus cameras (e.g., Topcon, Canon, Zeiss) is unverified and likely subject to domain shift.
intended_use: Investigational academic research prototype for biomedical microvascular hypothesis generation. Strictly not for clinical diagnosis, patient triage, or medical decision-making.
